decisions.final:
Concept tested: the blanket-ban verdict and its reasoning. Intuition: a ban you cannot enforce is not a ban. Users trade on unregulated exchanges to bypass sanctions and capital flow restrictions, providers relocate to lighter jurisdictions, and VPNs hide locations. The recommended alternative is targeted restriction: for example, restricting crypto derivatives (Japan, UK) or restricting crypto as payment for goods and services, which can work in the SHORT run.

(d) is correct. A general ban is likely ineffective in both horizons because monitoring and enforcement are difficult.

notes: The PDF could not be rendered (no pdftoppm and no Python PDF library), so the per-page text layer in scratchpad/ci_full.txt was used. All three flagged strings are in it verbatim. A scan of the whole slice for '(a) <lowercase>' found no other article slips. Five items were spot-checked (CI-I-47 balance-sheet limits, CI-I-65 BCBS two groups with 1,250% on max(long, short), CI-I-74 multicloud and the ~80% outage figure, CI-I-79 apparent suppression of the run and the case for ABMs, CI-I-86 SITIs and the principles-based caveat). In all five the key, solution and option analysis are correct and match the source. The keys are heavily skewed: 37 of 43 are (a). That comes from the source (the ANSWER lines match) and is a position bias for learning, not an error.
